rv.q: The new numbers that she's written for "9 to 5," sad to say, are slick and untheatrical.
'9 to 5' is a female-empowerment theme-park musical - complete with a spunky Dolly Parton impersonator and lots of faceless scenery.

"In the current Roundabout Theatre Company production at Studio 54-the former disco is an ironic location for this desolate comedy-drama-director Anthony Page and his brilliant cast neatly sidestep that pitfall and dance a merry gig around it.
The ones in this presentation work very well for me.
Folks yearning for an old-fashioned musical may finally get their wish as the 1980 movie "9 to 5" arrives on Broadway.
Director Anthony Page has created a fantasy slice of life that bursts vividly out of the bubble of the viewer's imagination.

cn.t: Lane and Irwin lead a brilliant cast in a production that finds both comic joy and crushing despair in Beckett's masterwork, with directors and performers making strong interpretive choices that resonate.

sg.ra: SeatPlan names Center Orchestra rows E-G as the best seats overall, citing 'a winning mix of perfect proximity and elevated view over the heads in front' on a good rake with a low stage. Headout notes the 'outstanding inclination' keeps sightlines clear from middle rows. AVFMS Row D seat 2: 'Perfect view with unlimited legroom.' 16-row section seats ~350 of the 413 total; low stage means front rows don't require neck strain.

SeatPlan explicitly names Left and Right Mezzanine as 'the best value seats at the Laura Pels Theatre,' citing cheap tickets vs. central Orchestra with 'a clear and close view.' Only 3 rows (AA/BB/CC), under 100 seats — feels intimate and close to stage. Headout confirms 'very little restriction from the Mezzanine overhang at the back' of the Orchestra, meaning the Mezzanine itself is close/low. Row BB flagged by Headout as a specific value row.
